extracted.intended_audience: immigrants, advocates, and members of the public submitting a public comment on the USCIS immigrant registry rule
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to for drafting and filing a public comment opposing the USCIS immigrant registry (USCIS-2025-0004-0001), balancing personalization with commenter safety and anonymity. Includes step-by-step submission actions, deadline, and content framing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the eight-step submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Step-by-step actions listed as: 1) Prepare your comment using the provided template; 2) Access Regulations.gov at the rule page (USCIS-2025-0004-0001); 3) Click the Comment button; 4) Enter your comment in the text field; 5) Paste your prepared text; 6) Select Anonymous under the identity question; 7) Complete the reCAPTCHA; 8) Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this exact sequence when filing on Regulations.gov. Particular actionable items: go to the specified docket (USCIS-2025-0004-0001), use the site UI's 'Comment' button and text field, paste prepared text rather than typing in to avoid mistakes, select 'Anonymous' for identity, complete reCAPTCHA before final submission. The procedural list is the primary checklist to successfully file the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit before the stated date/time; late comments may not be considered. The deadline is a hard constraint for participation in the rulemaking docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize anonymity to protect safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity: explicitly recommended to protect commenters' safety. United We Dream advises selecting 'Anonymous' under the identity question on Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For immigrants, especially those with vulnerability to enforcement or retaliation, choose anonymity even if typical guidance suggests identifying yourself. Selecting 'Anonymous' hides identifying metadata and reduces risk. This is an explicit safety-first recommendation that overrides standard 'identify yourself' guidance for at-risk populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize your comment with lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "Don't forget to make it personal — your story and feelings matter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include personal stories and emotional stakes to make the comment compelling. However, balance personalization with safety: preserve the texture of lived experience (details, feelings, impact) while omitting identifying metadata (names, exact addresses, immigration identifiers). The page recommends anonymized-but-personalized comments — retain voice and specifics that convey harm without revealing identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the provided template and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare your comment using the provided template. The Template Framework emphasizes opposition to the registry's discriminatory nature, historical parallels to harmful registration systems, the rule as a 'registration trap' forcing self-identification, and calls for rescinding the rule and expanding immigrant protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the recommended rhetorical frames: characterize the rule as discriminatory; draw comparisons to historical harmful registration systems to illustrate risks; label the policy a 'registration trap' that coerces self-identification; explicitly demand rescission and stronger immigrant protections. Using the template ensures messaging consistency and aligns comments with advocacy goals. Customize wording to your experience while keeping these central frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance standard comment best-practices with safety constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner insight: For vulnerable populations, the standard advice ('personalize, identify yourself, give specifics') collides with safety. United We Dream's solution: anonymized but personalized comments — preserve the texture of lived experience without the identifying metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing effective comments, ordinarily include identifying information and specifics to increase credibility; but for at-risk commenters, explicitly avoid identifying metadata and instead convey particulars in non-identifying ways (e.g., describe types of harm, approximate timelines, general locations). This entry functions as decision guidance on how to adapt best-practices under safety constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: File on the correct docket/rule page
rubrics_metrics.description: Access Regulations.gov at the rule page (USCIS-2025-0004-0001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are submitting to the precise docket so your comment is associated with the correct rulemaking record. Using the specified docket identifier avoids misfiling and ensures the comment will be considered in the immigrant registry rule's administrative record.
